Class AcceptedMediaTypes

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.web.router.AcceptedMediaTypes
@Internal public final class AcceptedMediaTypes extends Object
The checks of the accepted media types that take a quality of 0 into account: an accepted media range with q=0 means "not acceptable", see RFC 9110, section 12.4.2.
Since:
5.3.0
Author:
Denis Stepanov

    • negotiate

      public static @Nullable MediaType negotiate(List<MediaType> produces, boolean producesAll, @Nullable Collection<MediaType> accepted)
      Negotiates the type of a response: for each accepted range, by the preference of the client, the first produced type that it covers and that is acceptable, else, for a route that produces all types, the first concrete acceptable accepted type. A route that produces all types answers in its default type, JSON, whenever it is acceptable, as it does without accepted types of the quality 0: the body might not be encodable in another type.
      Parameters:
      produces - The types the route produces, */* producing JSON
      producesAll - Whether the route produces all types
      accepted - The accepted types, ordered by the preference of the client
      Returns:
      The negotiated type, null when no type is acceptable, the first produced type without accepted types

    • intersects

      public static boolean intersects(MediaType type, Collection<MediaType> accepted)
      Whether a type, possibly a range, has an acceptable intersection with the accepted types: an accepted range covers it and it is acceptable, or it is a range that covers an accepted type that is acceptable. No default type is substituted for a range.
      Parameters:
      type - A type or a range, such as text/* or */*
      accepted - The accepted types
      Returns:
      Whether some type of the intersection is acceptable

    • isAcceptable

      public static boolean isAcceptable(MediaType produced, @Nullable Collection<MediaType> accepted)
      Whether a produced media type is acceptable: the most specific accepted media range that covers it decides, a range of the quality 0 rejecting it. A produced media range is acceptable when it covers an accepted type with a quality above 0.
      Parameters:
      produced - The produced media type
      accepted - The accepted media types
      Returns:
      Whether the produced type is acceptable, true without accepted types
